jamal: @channel Quietwindow exercise scheduled SAT 03:00–04:30 UTC. We're running a controlled burst-drain + cross-AZ failover to validate SLO fallback policies and QoS prioritization. Expected: short p99 latency blips (~+40–80ms) and temporary throttling on best-effort buckets. No planned 5xx. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/quietwindow-2025 (ID RW-QW-2025)

jamal: Plan highlights:
• 03:00 — start traffic shift: 20% -> west-1 standby (canary) for 30m
• 03:30 — induce controlled node drains in west-1 for two GPU pools (burst-drain)
• 03:45 — failover routing to east-1 for remaining traffic, validate KV cache warmup
• 04:15 — gradual restore, monitor SLO and rollback if errors >0.5% or p99 spike >200ms for >5m

jamal: Quick ops commands (use infra-cli):
```
infra-cli drain-pool --pool gpu-west1-burst --concurrency 50 --dry-run=false
infra-cli shift-traffic --from west-1 --to west-1-canary --percent 20
redwood-slo check --route chat-gen --window 5m
```

maria: oncall acked. I'll be sitting on the channel for the whole window. @jamal please DM the canary list so I can watch dashboards. :eyes:

jamal: Canary services: model-serving-proxy (v2.1.3), kvcache-front (sticky), router-west1-canary. I'll DM the exact host IDs.

alex: infra notes: we'll pre-set capacity-override=2x for Dedicated pools in west-1 earlier today, and disable autoscale for those pools during the window. Also will temporarily raise eviction backoff to avoid noisy node churn.

devon: quick Q — any client-facing SLA/notice?

ken: product — we're not planning a broad customer banner for this exercise. If we see >10m of meaningful latency regression, we'll surface a short banner and email enterprise customers with active Dedicated contracts. I'll standby to draft.

jamal: Also patching SLO guardrails for the window: we'll accept a temporary p99 delta allowance +20ms for the exercise and annotate it in the SLO dashboard. This is strictly for monitoring/alert suppression only; we won't permanently change targets.

slo-signal-bot: NOTICE: Temporary SLO allowance applied for route=chat-gen p99 +20ms from 1788888123 to 1788889050 (reason: Quietwindow exercise).

oncall-bot: Incident stub created: RW-QW-2025-EX (quietwindow exercise) — monitor channel #eng-sre. Runbook linked.

maria: thumbs up. I'll focus on error budget and latency panels. If any request rates drop >15% or 5xx rate >0.2% jump, I'll trigger rollback.

alex: we'll emit a structured trace tag for all canary requests: header X-RW-Quietwindow: canary-1788 so DevEx and tracing can filter.

devon: Will do a quick smoke on the SDKs to ensure reconnect/backoff behaviours are fine. If anyone sees SDK issues, tag me.

jamal: Post-mortem cadence: brief notes in runbook within 24h, full aftermarket review if anything >0.5% user-impact. Otherwise a short summary to eng-all.

ken: thanks — if all good, this validates QoS buckets and gives us stronger evidence for Dedicated fallback guarantees.

scheduler-bot: Reminder set — Quietwindow exercise starts in 48h (1789050000).

maria: final ask — folks owning models please ensure pinned-versions are set; warmup prompts for large-context models would help reduce p99 on failover.

jamal: noted. I'll post a quick checklist tomorrow AM with host IDs and exact rollback commands. Thanks everyone. :rocket:
